home.lead: A dual-core 240 MHz computer with Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, on a board the size of a finger.

board.title: Board
board.text: The DevKitC: USB ports, buttons, a regulator and two rows of header pins around one module.

module.title: Module
module.text: The WROOM module: the chip, its flash and PSRAM, a crystal and the antenna, under one metal can.

can.title: Under the can
can.text: Lift the shield and the parts appear: the ESP32-S3 package sits next to its memory and the 40 MHz crystal.

package.title: Package
package.text: A 7 × 7 mm QFN with 56 pads: every pin you wire on the header ends at one of them.

die.title: Die
die.text: The silicon itself, drawn as 32 blocks by family. The ones your labs have used stand taller.

home.sentence: Your labs have used {{used}} of {{total}} blocks.
home.nextNone: Every block the labs reach is done. The rest wait for new labs.

atlas.lead: All {{count}} blocks of the ESP32-S3, grouped by family. Taller tiles on the die and a state on each card show how far the labs have taken them.

pins.lead: {{count}} GPIOs, each with several jobs. Our labs have wired {{used}} of them.
pins.legend: Emphasised rows are pins our labs used; a triangle marks a pin hazard.
pins.matrix: Each GPIO and the kinds of function it can take
pins.pickHint: Pick a pin to see its functions, its strapping role and the hazards that apply to it.
pins.pickLegend: Bar under a number: used in our labs. Corner triangle: a pin hazard. Dashed: not on the header.
pins.offHeader: Not on the DevKitC header: it belongs to the module's flash or PSRAM.
pins.strappingLead: These pins are read the instant the chip leaves reset. Whatever you wire to them must not pull them the wrong way at power-up.
pins.gotchasLead: A few pins have a job before your code runs, or belong to something else. The rest of the rules hold for every pin.

inside.lead: Where your code and data live, which clock drives what, and how much each power mode saves.

memory.title: The address map
memory.lead: The CPU sees one big address space: ROM, internal SRAM, the flash and PSRAM through the caches, and the peripherals' registers.
memory.caption: The ESP32-S3 address map, low addresses at the top

clocks.title: The clock tree
clocks.lead: One 40 MHz crystal feeds a PLL; dividers make the CPU, APB and peripheral clocks from it, while slow RC oscillators keep the RTC ticking in sleep.
clocks.caption: Clock sources, dividers and the blocks they clock

power.title: Power modes
power.lead: Each step down the ladder switches more of the chip off, and the current drops by orders of magnitude.
power.caption: Typical current in each power mode, on a log scale, and what stays on
